title: Whales are Capable of Complex Communication — Could Humans Ever Talk With Them?
titleZh: 人类能与鲸类进行跨物种沟通吗
summary:
鲸类是地球上智力最高的物种之一。从抹香鲸、座头鲸到虎鲸（其严格分类属于海豚科），每个鲸类物种都拥有独特的交流系统，甚至同一物种的不同族群之间，声讯交流也各有差异。随着人类对这些交流方式进行长期研究与观测，一个问题逐渐浮现：未来，人类能否与鲸类实现声学层面的互动？而这种互动，又能为我们理解非人类智慧提供怎样的线索？围绕这些议题，加州大学戴维斯分校的Whale-SETI团队与阿拉斯加鲸类基金会的研究人员，以座头鲸为研究对象，持续探索鲸与人类之间的声学交流，并已得出一些引人入胜的发现。

来源：Discover；作者：Sara Novak；原文发布时间：2026-02-06 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Whales are some of the most highly intelligent species on Earth. Each species of whale, from sperm whales to humpback whales to orcas (which are technically dolphins), has a distinct communication system that often varies within populations. Since humans have been researching and observing these forms of communication, a question has surfaced: Could humans one day engage in acoustic interactions with whales? And what could these interactions reveal about non-human intelligence? Researchers from the Whale-SETI team at the University of California, Davis, and the Alaska Whale Foundation have been exploring whale-to-human communication with humpback whales, and they’ve come up with some fascinating conclusions.
paragraphs.contentZh: 鲸类是地球上智力最高的物种之一。从抹香鲸、座头鲸到虎鲸（其严格分类属于海豚科），每个鲸类物种都拥有独特的交流系统，甚至同一物种的不同族群之间，声讯交流也各有差异。随着人类对这些交流方式进行长期研究与观测，一个问题逐渐浮现：未来，人类能否与鲸类实现声学层面的互动？而这种互动，又能为我们理解非人类智慧提供怎样的线索？围绕这些议题，加州大学戴维斯分校的Whale-SETI团队与阿拉斯加鲸类基金会的研究人员，以座头鲸为研究对象，持续探索鲸与人类之间的声学交流，并已得出一些引人入胜的发现。

paragraphs.contentEn: When scientists recorded a humpback whale contact call, known as a whup, and played it underwater around their research vessel, they were surprised when a whale named Twain became a more than willing participant in the call-and-response exchange. Scientists produced a single sound, or whup call, that Twain would then respond with her own whup call to them, a "conversation" described in their PeerJ paper.
paragraphs.contentZh: 当研究人员录制下一种被称为“whup”的座头鲸联络叫声，并在研究船附近的水下播放时，一头名叫吐温的座头鲸的反应令他们惊喜，它不仅没有回避，反而主动加入了这场呼唤与回应的互动。研究人员每播放一次“whup”声，吐温都会以自己的“whup”叫声回应，在发表于《PeerJ》期刊的论文中，研究人员将这种一来一回的声学互动描述为一场“对话”。

paragraphs.contentEn: “It might loosely translate to ‘hello’ or some sort of greeting call for when animals come together or just to signal that individuals are in a certain location,” says Josephine Hubbard, study author and animal behaviorist with Whale SETI. In this case, it was as if Twain was either saying “hello” to scientists or “I’m over here.” But in both instances, she was responding to and engaging with whale signals that humans produced. Additionally, it’s worth noting that to call it a “conversation” is also interesting because human linguists would have a specific definition of what a conversation actually is, says Hubbard.
paragraphs.contentZh: Whale-SETI团队的动物行为学家、该研究的作者约瑟芬·哈伯德解释道：“这种叫声大致可以理解为一种‘你好’，或是在鲸群聚集时发出的一种问候信号，也可能只是用来标示自己的位置。”在这次实验中，吐温的回应就像是在对研究人员说“你好”，或表示“我在这里”。但无论具体含义为何，她显然是在对人类播放的鲸类信号作出主动回应并与之互动。哈伯德进一步指出，将这一过程称作“对话”本身已具有意义，因为人类语言学家对“对话”其实有着严格且明确的定义。

paragraphs.contentEn: Of course, whether whales want to communicate with humans varies by the temperament of the whale and by the situation. Just like some humans are more extroverted than others, this could also be true for whales, although this would need more research to understand. Twain circled around the scientists’ boat and was in proximity to its speakers. Permit limitations only allow for researchers to produce the sound for 20 minutes, but once they stopped, Twain continued to produce more signals before leaving. “What’s cool about Twain is that she could have left at any point, as it wasn’t a captive environment where she couldn’t leave, so she was choosing to be close to us,” says Hubbard.
paragraphs.contentZh: 当然，鲸类是否愿意与人类交流，取决于个体的性情以及具体情境。正如人类性格有外向与内向之分，鲸类之间或许也存在类似差异，不过这一点仍有待进一步研究证实。在这次实验中，吐温围绕研究船游动，并多次接近船体下方的水下扬声器。按照研究许可的限制，科研人员只能播放这种叫声20分钟，当他们停止播放后，吐温仍持续发出回应信号，一段时间后才离开现场。哈伯德指出：“吐温这一行为值得关注的地方在于，她本可以在任何时候离开，因为这不是一个她无法脱身的圈养环境，但她选择留在我们附近。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Humpback whales also produce “bubble rings,” in many cases in close proximity to boats, in ways that suggest that they’re being playful and that whales are doing it in a relaxed manner. Another paper published last year by Hubbard and her team in the journal Marine Mammal Science analyzed 39 rings made by 11 individual whales that suggest a playful, communicative side to the whales. “These new observations show humpback whales producing bubble rings during friendly encounters with humans,” write the study authors.
paragraphs.contentZh: 除了声音交流，座头鲸还会制造“气泡圈”，在许多情况下，它们会在船只附近制造气泡圈，其行为方式表明它们正处于嬉戏玩耍的状态，且整个行为过程是放松的。去年，哈伯德及其团队在《海洋哺乳动物科学》期刊发表的一项研究中，对11头座头鲸制造的39个气泡圈进行了分析，结果显示，这一行为可能反映出座头鲸具有嬉戏和交流的一面。研究作者在论文中写道：“这些新的观测记录表明，座头鲸在与人类进行友好接触时会制造气泡圈。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Often, a willingness to communicate with humans would be food-mediated, but in this case, it wasn’t. There have also been other examples. Gray whales in the San Ignacio lagoon in Mexico, for example, are famously friendly. In fact, some gray whales regularly approach boats and allow visitors to have gentle contact with them.
paragraphs.contentZh: 通常情况下，野生动物愿意与人类互动，往往与食物有关，但这次案例中并不存在这种诱因。类似的情形此前也曾发生，例如生活在墨西哥圣伊格纳西奥泻湖的灰鲸就以对人类友善而闻名。事实上，一些灰鲸会定期主动靠近船只，甚至允许游客轻轻触碰它们。

paragraphs.contentEn: According to the Oceanic Society, this behavior isn’t shared amongst all gray whales, and in fact, this species of whale was almost hunted to extinction just a generation ago. But the behavior may have been passed down through generations, and some gray whales in this population voluntarily approach humans. In the end, these and other encounters show that, in some cases, individual whales appear willing to engage with humans. And the more we learn about their mode of communication and what they are saying to us, the more we can learn about them.
paragraphs.contentZh: 根据海洋协会的资料，这种亲近人类的行为并非所有灰鲸都有，实际上，就在一代人之前，这一鲸种还因捕猎而濒临灭绝。但研究人员认为，此类行为可能通过代际传递留存下来，使得该种群中部分灰鲸至今仍会主动靠近人类。上述及其他案例表明，在特定情境下，某些鲸类个体似乎确实愿意与人类互动。随着我们对其交流方式及其传递信息的理解逐渐加深，人类也将更深入地认识这些海洋中的智慧生命。
